options.label: The Rush (Vote Tuesday at 1:00 p.m.)
options.description: Proceed immediately to vote on rejecting Corvane and awarding the contract to Tasker & Moye before the protest response deadline expires on Tuesday.

options.label: The Cure (Contact Corvane for Immediate Fix)
options.description: Contact Corvane Builders immediately to request proof of licensed subcontractors and an acknowledgment of Addendum No. 2 before the Board votes, attempting to cure the bid's deficiencies.

options.label: The Pause (Postpone Vote Entirely)
options.description: Postpone the Board's award vote until Friday, October 30, or the following week to allow time for the protest resolution, late supplement review, and full compliance with procedural timelines.

options.label: The Split Vote (Preliminary Decision + Later Award)
options.description: Issue a written preliminary decision rejecting Corvane as nonresponsive immediately (Monday/Tuesday) to resolve the protest, then schedule the Board's final award vote for later in the week (Wednesday–Friday) after all procedural requirements are met.

options.label: The Rush (Vote Tuesday at 1:00 p.m.)
options.note: This option violates the mandatory two-day response window mandated by ITB § 21.5, creating an immediate risk of a successful writ of mandate that would vacate the award and delay the project indefinitely.

options.label: The Cure (Contact Corvane for Immediate Fix)
options.note: Allowing a bidder to cure a nonresponsive bid after the submission deadline constitutes impermissible post-bid negotiation and material alteration of the bid, which is strictly prohibited under public procurement law and would invalidate the entire bidding process.

options.label: The Pause (Postpone Vote Entirely)
options.note: While legally defensible as a way to ensure full procedural compliance, this option unnecessarily stalls the project schedule and fails to utilize the Board's authority to make a preliminary determination on responsiveness, thereby delaying the resolution of the protest without a clear benefit.

options.label: The Split Vote (Preliminary Decision + Later Award)
options.note: This option correctly balances legal compliance with the client's schedule by allowing the Board to act on the nonresponsiveness issue immediately after the response deadline while preserving the right to a formal hearing on the broader responsibility issues before final award.

grade.missing: An experienced practitioner would have explicitly distinguished between the 'nonresponsiveness' grounds (license and addendum), which can be decided summarily by the Board, and the 'responsibility' ground (past termination), which legally requires a formal hearing with notice and an opportunity to be heard before a final adverse determination.
grade.overall: The best option is to issue a preliminary decision on the nonresponsive grounds immediately after the response deadline and schedule a separate hearing for the responsibility issue, as this approach strictly adheres to statutory timelines while avoiding the legal pitfalls of post-bid cures or premature final awards. This strategy protects the District from a successful writ of mandate while keeping the project on track to award the contract to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder as soon as the hearing record is complete.
